references.text: The angel of the Lord later explains that he stood in the way as an adversary (satan) to Balaam, the same motif as in verse 22
The angel of the Lord reveals himself in a similar manner by standing in the way before people
God's wrath burns against one who is on a journey, parallel to God's wrath against Balaam on the road
The angel of the Lord stands in the way and reveals himself, a theophany similar to that in the Balaam narrative
Satan rises up against Israel, using the same Hebrew root (שָׂטָן) as in Numbers 22:22
Satan (הַשָּׂטָן) is presented as an adversary, the same word stem that describes the angel's role toward Balaam
Satan as adversary, related to the angel's function as 'satan' (adversary) for Balaam
The angel of the Lord and Satan are mentioned together, showing the development of the concept from Numbers 22:22
Peter refers to Balaam who left the right way, noting that he was rebuked for his transgression
Balaam's way is cited as a warning example of error for financial gain
Balaam's teaching is mentioned as a warning, referring back to the entire Balaam narrative
